title.narrative: COVID-19: Active Response and Expenditure Support Program

description.narrative: The program supports the government's COVID-19 pandemic response plan, of which the ACF is the predominant part, to help mitigate the adverse impacts of COVID-19 on the population's health, incomes, and economic opportunities as well as macroeconomic stability. The outcome will be the COVID-19 outbreak more effectively managed and its adverse social and economic impacts reduced.

National poverty rate is maintained at or below the pre-COVID-19 level by 31 December 2021. Progress/Status: Status: Awaiting data
42. The 2018 and 2019 national poverty rates were estimated by the State Committee on Statistics (SCS) as 11.4 percent and 11.0 percent . The target for 31 December 2020 is 11.4 percent. The SCS national poverty rate data for 2020 will not be available until February 2021, and since other estimates of poverty rate are not consistent/compatible with that used by the SCS, assessment of the performance measure must wait until then. 43. Using a different measure, the WHO/UN reports on Uzbekistan estimated that the poverty rate rose to between 8.7 and 10 percent following the outbreak, compared to pre-COVID estimates of 7.4 percent . This put between 450,000 and 880,000 additional people in poverty.
(Q3 2020 CARES Report received on 16 Nov 2020) Data Source: Reports from the Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Economic Development and Poverty Reduction and World Bank country reports Actual value:

COVID-19 confirmed cases doubling rate reduced to at least 30 days or more by 31 December 2020. Progress/Status: Status: Target achieved
The estimated doubling rate for COVID-19 confirmed cases has moved from 17 days on 9 July 2020 to 140 days on 28 October 2019, against a target of 30 days by 31 December 2020. Performance is significantly better than the target which indicates that, at the moment, the virus is under improved control. There is no sex and/or age disaggregated data available to measure the case doubling rate by gender and/or age.
(Q3 2020 CARES Report received on 16 Nov 2020) Data Source: Reports from the Ministry of Health and World Health Organization country reports Actual value:

At least 75% of SMEs remained in business by 31 December 2021. Progress/Status: Status: Target achieved
The number of SMEs in business was reported as 391,300 on 1 October 2020 and 370,358 1 July 2020 , both of which are higher than the number at the baseline date, which was 352,167 on 1st of April 2020. The true measure of this indicator may not be available until 2021 and requires further validation given that a SME that has ceased to trade will not automatically close or declare itself as not remaining in business. The percentage of SMEs that are owned by women is 9.8%. Information on the percentage of SMEs that are owned or managed by women has been requested and is awaited.
(Q3 2020 CARES Report received on 16 Nov 2020) Data Source: Reports from the Agency for Development of Small Business and Entrepreneurship and State Committee on Statistics and World Bank country reports Actual value:

Output: COVID-19 response and health system strengthening measures implemented Indicator: At least 500 ventilators, 250,000 testing kits, and appropriately sized personal protective gear, including gender-responsive individual packages for female health workers, delivered to identified medical facilities Progress/Status: Status: Target achieved
By end of October 2020, 1662 ventilators had been received, of which 1,362 had been delivered to site. This compares with a DMF target of 500 ventilators by 31 December 2020. A further 419 ventilators are scheduled to arrive by the end of the year. 51. From July 2020, Uzbekistan started domestic mass production of COVID-19 test kits. This was announced by the Ministry of Innovative Development. The test kits are manufactured by the LLC ‘Biotest-LAB' at the Centre for Advanced Technologies. The Ministry announced that the production capacity is over 500,000 test kits per month. The Ministry of Health has procured PPE for health workers who are providing medical service to COVID-19 patients, including with support for international development partners. New standards have been adopted for production and procurement of the facial masks, protection clothing, antiseptic devices: (i) 3 national standards for medical masks from non-woven fabric, developed on the basis of the European EN standard, gauze masks, shoe covers and medical caps; (ii) 5 international ISO and EN standards for various types of protective clothing; and 24 units ASTM standard, establishing requirements for special protective clothing (face masks, gloves, surgical gowns) and methods for testing it. A domestic enterprises have reprofiled their activities and developed the production of PPEs (masks, protective clothing, antiseptics). As of October 2020, Ministry of Health has been requested to provide up-to-date data on the numbers of testing kits and PPEs that have been delivered to health workers, including sex-disaggregated data.
(Source: Q3 CARES Report received on 16 Nov 2020) Data Source: Reports from the Ministry of Health and World Health Organization country reports Actual value:

Output: Dedicated social safety net funds for social protection and compensation for economic losses of low-income households expanded Indicator: Number of low-income households receiving childcare and social benefits increased by at least 10%, with priority given to single mothers, divorced women, and widows. Progress/Status: Status: Partially Achieved.
The target is 654,940 households for 31 December 2020, against a baseline figure of 595,400 at March 2020. Information from Information from Ministry of Makhalla (Jan-July 2020) shows that 663,038 households have received low-income subsidies.
A recent data provided by the Citizens Budget shows that total number of families receiving childcare allowance for children below 2 years of age, families receiving benefits for children under 14 years of age and low income families receiving financial aid increased by 40% (exceeding the target of 10% increase) from 595,439 to 832,839 and total budget expenditures increased from UZS 2.8 trillion to UZS3,9 trillion in 2020 considering anti-crisis measures. Other support to women also provided under the Council of the Federation of Trade Unions from the Anti-Crisis Fund.
The required data broken down by the status of the women is not directly measured by the line ministries or SCS however eligibility criteria will be verified from the ministries or SCS.

Output: Affected sectors and businesses supported to prevent job losses from the economic downturn Indicator: An additional SUM500 billion provided to the State Fund for Support of Entrepreneurship to provide guarantees and compensation of interest expenses for SMEs, of which at least 40% are women-owned and/or managed Progress/Status: Status: Partially Achieved. Information provided by MOF in November 2020 shows that to date, from the State Fund for Support of Entrepreneurship (SFSE), under the Agency for Development of Small Business, entrepreneurs have received financial assistance in the amount of UZS 8.4 trillion for loans worth UZS 39.9 trillion allocated for a total of 24,400 projects, resulting in the creation of 191,800 new jobs. The amount of UZS 8.4 trillion financial assistance greatly exceeds the DMF target of UZS 500 billion.
In particular, the following have been awarded: • Guarantees worth UZS 4.9 trillion for the allocation of UZS 12.8 trillion of credit for 6,600 projects; • UZS 3.5 trillion compensation to repay part of the interest on loans worth UZS 27.1 trillion for 17,800 projects; • UZS 33.4 billion of preferential resources for 49 projects for the allocation of soft loans worth UZS 35.0 billion.
For the period January 1 to October 1, 2020, a total of 16,673 people received guarantees and compensations from the SFSE, of which 1,585 were women (9.5%) . This is a different figure from the number of businesses owned or managed by women, which is a much higher figure, targeted at 40%.
Data on benefits funds allocated from the ACF is not fully disaggregated by gender. One exception is the use of funds received from the ACF by JSCB Agrobank. These funds were used to open a credit line to support low-income families in the Republic of Karakalpakstan and to provide employment for school graduates in Andijan region by offering business start-up loans. In both cases, although more women received benefits, men received between 45% and 47% more per head than women.
(Source: Q3 2020 CARES Report received on 16 Nov 2020) Data Source: Reports from the Ministry of Finance and Agency for Development of Small Business and Entrepreneurship, and World Bank country reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y

Output: Affected sectors and businesses supported to prevent job losses from the economic downturn Indicator: SUM3.6 trillion from the ACF spent on small- scale public works in the regions to create temporary jobs, at least 75% of which employ members of low-income households Progress/Status: Status: Partially Achieved.
The ACF budget shows that a total of UZS3.6 trillion is planned to be allocated to the Public Works Fund for public works in the regions (rehabilitation of urban, agriculture, sanitation and health, and education-related facilities) and small industrial zones. The report on the allocation of funds from the ACF. shows that this target has been achieved for funds allocated. The total amount allocated so far is UZS 3.8 trillion. However, information on how much has been actually spent on these works is required from the recipients of the funds.
270,549 women have been engaged in public works during 2020 and 171,408 young people (no sex-disaggregated data available). A total of UZB 470 billion have been allocated to this, including UZB 300 from the ACF.
Additionally, 17,767 women and 12,365 young people (no sex-disaggregated data available) have been subsidized by employment promotion centers for 2020. A total of UZS 150 billion have been allocated to subsidies, including UZB 105 billion from the ACF.
(Source: Q3 2020 CARES Report received on 16 Nov 2020) Data Source: Reports from the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Employment and Labor Relations, and State Committee on Statistics and World Bank country reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y

Output: Affected sectors and businesses supported to prevent job losses from the economic downturn Indicator: Sector-specific tax and other incentives (i.e., exemptions, lower tax rates, tax holidays, and loan repayment deferments) for SMEs provided, of which at least 40% are women-owned and/or managed Progress/Status: Status: Target achieved
The social contributions tax for individual entrepreneurs has been reduced by 50% (from 12% to 6%) from 1 April to 1 October 2020. Payments of personal income tax, and social tax for individual entrepreneurs and SMEs, have been suspended with interest-free deferment until 1 October 2020. SMEs and businesses in services, transportation, tourism and aviation are exempted from property and land taxes and will pay a reduced social contributions tax (1% instead of 12%). The State Tax Committee will suspend tax audits until 1 January 2021. The filing of personal income tax declarations for fiscal year 2019 has been postponed from 1 April 2020 to 1 August 2020. Local governments will reduce taxes by 30%, provide a 6-month grace period for paying property and land taxes and fees for water use, and suspend the accrual of tourist (hotel) tax from April until October 2020. The Ministry of Finance (MOF) will compensate the loss of revenue to local governments. The tax rate for water use on agricultural irrigated land was reduced by 50%. The deadlines for audit reports are extended until 1 October 2020. These measures will cost UZS4.2 trillion. There is no sex/age disaggregated data available to measure which groups of the population have benefited from the tax measures.
Presidential Decree №5996, 18 May 2020: Property tax and land tax are exempted for the period from June 1 to September 1, 2020 for: • small business entities; • markets and shopping malls, cinemas, catering, public transport, sports and fitness facilities, as well as legal entities engaged in the transportation of passengers, the provision of household services, the provision of rental premises, including for banquets. Additional state support in the form of write-offs are provided for: • property tax and land tax payable for April and May 2020, for which interest-free deferral was provided in accordance with the PD#5969 and PD#5978; • penalties and fines for land tax and property tax, as of May 15, 2020, formed on January 1, 2020. Business entities are provided deferral of payment of VAT up to 120 days, when importing goods (works, services); Social tax rate reduced from 12% to 1% between May 1 and July 1, 2020 for micro-firms and small enterprises (except manufacturers of excisable goods, state enterprises, legal entities with more than 50% state share in authorized capital); Credits for construction and reconstruction of individual houses at the expense of MOF resources are to be implemented as an experiment.
Presidential Decree № 6029, July 2020: From July 1 until December 31, 2020: • public catering enterprises and entities specializing in the provision of premises for rent are exempted from paying turnover tax; • individuals are exempt from paying tax on income received from the lease of real estate; • the procedure of applying the minimum rental rates for tax purposes is suspended for individuals who rent out property (premises and motor vehicles); • catering establishments are exempt from paying fees for the right to carry out retail trade in alcoholic products from Apr 1, 2020 until Dec 31, 2020; The period of tax benefits and preferences that are already in effect is extended until December 31, 2020: • small business entities and markets as well as shopping malls, cinemas, catering, public transport, sports and fitness facilities, legal entities engaged in the transportation of passengers, the provision of household and rental services are exempt from property tax and land tax; • social tax rate reduced from 12% to 1% between May 1 and July 1, 2020 for micro-firms aand small enterprises; • deferred payment of customs duties and excise taxes levied on the import of goods provided to micro-firms and small enterprises within 120 days.
(Source: Q3 2020 CARES Report received on 16 Nov 2020) Data Source: Reports from the Ministry of Finance, State Statistics Committee, and the Agency for Development of Small Business and Entrepreneurship; and World Bank country reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y
